All actual values discovered/captured during contract inventory BEFORE tests; unresolved default stops approval, not deferred implementation judgment. Prefer nullable opt-in settings to changing AgentCliClientOptions default for all unrelated consumers.
Precedence explicit session override > caller legacy path/model ONLY when selected==caller configured default > strategy entry > strategy intrinsic default. Legacy applies to its associated default, never another selected strategy. When both strategy setting and same caller legacy nonempty, retain legacy precedence and emit safe deprecation notice; automatic migration writes explicit strategy entry and removes only task-approved matching legacy fields, preserving unrelated caller differences via caller-scoped strategy override map if values differ; conflicts require no data loss, caller override wins. Path/model are independent; explicit auto means no model argument only per strategy semantics. Validate key aliases normalized once; conflicting alias/canonical duplicates startup error. No basename guessing for explicit executable; mismatch delegated policy fails, never rewrite silently.
AgentHelp.RunAs is nullable string: null (including absent YAML) inherits TodoPrompts.RunAs; empty/whitespace disables; nonempty trimmed canonical account. Voice preserves existing TodoPrompts identity inheritance. TODO own RunAs preserved; pool/triage use their existing source if present, otherwise empty (do not introduce automatic sharpninja identity to every feature). Per-request parameter/env cannot set identity. For delegation, no API key/GH token/environment map passed over socket in v1, and caller configured injection => explicit IdentityDenied; local behavior remains. All caller sources inventoried before mock gate; any direct process caller configured Linux RunAs must verify same UID or reject until routed, never ignore.
Windows uses unchanged profile-environment mechanism; document not Unix impersonation. Other unsupported OS + nonempty RunAs fails capability; empty remains local. Linux account resolution failure -> IdentityInvalid, same effective UID verified -> local, other UID -> admin profile lookup and remote; no fallback. Model/executable requested must match selected policy entry; an explicit path equal approved source path is permitted, maps to policy-installed canonical artifact. No session-defined arbitrary executable admitted remotely.

## 5. Worker boundary and containment
New projects McpServer.AgentWorker (broker) and McpServer.AgentWorker.Runner (per-session local-strategy host) reference AgentExecution/Common only. Broker runs as target sharpninja in a user service under systemd --user; root-owned installed application/policy. Worker policy /etc/mcpserver/agent-worker/sharpninja.json root:root 0644; parent directories root-owned non-writable by mcpserver/sharpninja. Socket /run/mcpserver-agent-worker/sharpninja.sock directory target:worker-client-group 0750, socket target:worker-client-group 0660; group grants only mcpserver access, not arbitrary users. Actual authorized peer UID list explicit; same-account adversaries are outside Unix UID authentication guarantee. Broker checks SO_PEERCRED authorized UID before bytes; MCP checks socket parent ownership/mode/no symlinks and connected peer uid=profile ExpectedUid, not pathname alone. Policy SHA from admin profile must equal broker hash; mismatch fail.
Trust disclosure: target account owns its auth and can execute arbitrary software independently; this is bounded cooperative-agent lifecycle containment, NOT sandbox of malicious sharpninja or malicious CLI code. Do not claim cgroup prevents target user escaping to other user-manager units. Exe profiles are root-owned immutable CLI runtime snapshots staged by deployment, including launch script/interpreter/npm dependency closure for node shim tools; source-path alias maps approved original executable to installed manifest. Snapshot hash and permissions verify entire closure, refuse unresolved runtime/symlink dependency. User authentication remains user-owned; no credential copies, worker storage is not secret store. Workspace is canonical approved registered root and inode/symlink rules deny traversal aliases; workspace remains writable for real agent behavior only per existing strategy permission flags, no added always-approve. Target profile credential access is operator-approved.
Child environment is constructed empty then policy keys HOME,USER,LOGNAME,PATH,TMPDIR,XDG_RUNTIME_DIR,DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS,LANG only. HOME account database result; PATH snapshot runtime/bin plus /usr/bin:/bin, TMPDIR private mode0700 runtime. No inherited LD_*,NODE_OPTIONS,DOTNET_*,GH_TOKEN,model key or proxy variables. Model credentials read normally from target profile. Root-protected startup rejects unknown policy fields/invalid limits; bind session to policy revision; policy change drains old sessions then restart, no live partial reload. Validate immutable executable tree before startup and each spawn; directories not writable by caller/target to close writable-binary TOCTOU. Workspace canonical root plus user-trusted mutable contents is disclosed; policy validates root handle but does not promise immutable repo content.
Containment is implemented through injected IAgentProcessSupervisor; Local supervisor wraps existing spawner unchanged for nondelegated. Worker supervisor builds ProcessStartInfo with strategy argument list but launches using root-protected generic process runner through target user manager; no separate vendor CLI logic. API: StartAsync(AgentProcessLaunch,ct)->IAgentProcessLease; lease exposes ISpawnedProcess streams/status and CloseAsync(reason,timeout) returning CleanupReceipt; verified cleanup required before returning terminal result. Launch includes executableProfileId,argument vector FROM selected strategy, private working resource root; never receives raw request argv. Strategy still creates/reads its prompt/output files on target side; supervisor tracks private resource paths for crash recovery.
Per-session runner hosts the selected LOCAL CLI strategy and remains alive in Type=exec transient unit with ExitType=main, KillMode=control-group, TimeoutStartSec=10,TimeoutStopSec=5,RuntimeMaxSec=14410, NoNewPrivileges=true. Batch CLI invocations are launched in separate per-invocation transient units with generic process runner holding unit active after child exit until cleanup; interactive CLI has one invocation unit lasting its session. Process runner accepts only broker/runner internal validated launch frame, reports ready without launching, waits for ACK after exact unit/PID/cgroup capture, then launches requested strategy-built command. Actual CLI UID and PID captured before output accepted. No use of shell eval. Strategy process spawner adapter supplies pipes via existing ISpawnedProcess (sync Spawn compatibility bridged with bounded startup only; no async-over-sync deadlock on synchronization context). Isolated API contract/mock tests validate this adapter before code; timeout cancels pending start and cleans exact unit even if PID unknown.
Identity/cgroup ready deadline 10s; manager queries 2s each; start ACK once; terminate SIGTERM then manager SIGKILL with TimeoutStopSec5; stop verification 10s total; final drain5s. CLI operation deadline min(requested finite timeout, profile budget); default policy maximum14400s; helper120s preserved; negative timeout except infinite sentinel invalid. Independently enforced RuntimeMaxSec for child unit = permitted run budget+15s; idle interactive max1800s; session hard lifetime14400s. Units named mcp-agent-<policy-profile>-<epoch>-<session>-<invocation>. Generate no caller unit names. Before listening/recovery, sweep only owned prefix units and recorded resources, resolve pending start jobs, verify cgroups empty then delete resources. Cleanup failure stops admission and marks health unhealthy; normal final result not released before invocation cleanup for batch. Interactive keeps process alive until Escape (strategy semantics) or End; End verifies unit stop/descendants/files. On worker crash independent manager timer bounds lifetime, replacement worker must sweep before listen; user-manager/kernel unavailability blocks guarantee and requires operator recovery, no false completed receipt. Reparent/double-fork within unit tested; malicious deliberate cgroup escape outside claim.
Receipts contain epoch/session/op/invocation/profile/strategy/UID/PID/cgroup/exe-manifest hash/exit/cleanup booleans and times, never prompt/token/environment values. Success requires actual agent exit/result semantics and verified cleanup, not EOF/runner exit/PID disappearance. MemoryMax1GiB,TasksMax256,CPUQuota200%, one active operation globally, eight authenticated connections incl idle sessions, no unbounded queue; excess Busy explicit. Profile can lower but not increase compiled ceilings without new reviewed policy change.

## 6. Wire protocol and session semantics
One authenticated socket connection owns one session; no reconnection/resume/re-execution in v1. UUID session assigned worker, invocation per CLI execution, caller operation ids strictly monotonic UInt64 starting1 (control ids independent channel sequencing). Client is trusted MCP but all bytes validated. Frame 4-byte big-endian length then strict UTF8 JSON, camelCase ordinal keys, reject duplicates/unknown fields/NaN, maxDepth16, request<=1MiB, control<=16KiB,event<=64KiB. 5s absolute frame transfer deadline begins at first header byte (idle waiting for next frame governed session idle deadline, not five-second polling timeout); handshake10s from accept. Hello request {version:1,profileId,policySha256,selectedStrategy,workspaceId,model:string|null,agentName:string|null,initialPrompt,timeoutMilliseconds:long|null}; null timeout means profile max; target user/executable/env/outputPath are NOT payload fields. WorkspaceId maps to exact canonical root, executable profile selected by strategy policy. Client explicit path canonical policy-alias equality validated before hello and worker never uses caller path for execution. HelloAck {version,epoch,sessionId,policySha256,strategy,capabilities,workerUid,sequence:0}. Initial prompt stored privately; selected strategy creates session using requested prompt after ACK; interactive may launch immediately. Client rejects changed strategy/hash/UID.
Command envelope {version,epoch,sessionId,operationId,kind,body}; kind InitialRead,InitialStream,Send,SendStream,Escape,Cancel,End. Send body {prompt,timeoutMilliseconds}; read body {timeoutMilliseconds}; Escape body {}; Cancel body {targetOperationId}; End body {timeoutMilliseconds}. No malformed optional union fields accepted. Event {version,epoch,sessionId,operationId,sequence,kind,payload}; ProcessStarted {invocationId,agentPid,agentUid}; Output {stream:stdout|stderr|body,text}; ResultStart {state:Success|Error|Timeout|SpawnError,exitCode,contentType}; ResultChunk {field:body|stdout|stderr,text}; ResultEnd {cleanupReceiptId}; OperationCancelled {}; Error {code,correlationId}; SessionEnded {cleanupReceiptId}; State {alive,agentPid:null|positive,sessionStatus}. Result fields chunked, cap16MiB aggregate per op across body/stdout/stderr including duplicated representation; output callback streamed separately counts same raw bytes once in capture accounting, stored result fields count actual memory. Parsed is NOT serialized polymorphic CLR object: reconstruct existing parser from body/contentType, semantically same JSON/YAML parsed structure; typed data preservation tests mandatory.
First InitialRead or InitialStream consumes initial response exactly once; repeat=>ProtocolViolation. One response operation active per session; concurrent second returns Busy, no queued execution; global operation slot likewise. Send allowed only after initial operation returns successfully/nonfatal agent result and according to underlying strategy IsAlive semantics (batch permits another invocation even if IsAlive=false); Send does not require persistent process. Stream mode forwards existing yielded strings exactly, no fabricated token granularity; transport converts result/output events without double delivery. IAgentExecutionSession.AgentOutputReceived callback remains local callback replay for policy-approved outputs, not transmitted delegate; callback exceptions cancel op and clean session. Escape delegates current strategy method, no-op for strategies currently no-op; it is not transport cancellation. Cancel idempotent target current op; first terminal outcome wins cancellation/completion race under session lock. Cancellation of consuming operation sends Cancel, awaits bounded cleanup independent of caller ct, then throws OperationCanceledException locally. End/dispose idempotent, terminate active op/session; receive cleanup before acknowledgement. Client disconnect or stream-consumer abandonment cancels and ends session; no background orphan. Transport failures never retry an agent prompt automatically.
State machine Opening -> Open -> Active -> Open, or any live state -> Closing -> Closed/Faulted. Initial response consumed marker independent state. Batch process finished then PID retained as last observed agent PID, IsAlive false; next Send transitions PID on started event. Remote synchronous properties are latest observed snapshot, false/null before first started, no network query; heartbeat3s during active process, missing9s marks unknown-as-not-alive and cancels session (not proof process exited); operations surface WorkerUnavailable. One terminal event per op, sequence increments strict; duplicate/out-of-order/epoch mismatch closes and cleans; consumed op ids retained for current connection only, duplicate may return safe ProtocolViolation never rerun. No durable reconnect replay claim. Worker read and control handling independent bounded tasks; outbound queue max4events=256KiB, output total16MiB, stall frame deadline -> cleanup. Redaction constant transport/policy errors, never log requests/argv containing prompts or secrets.

## 7. BDPv4 increments, mock validation and evidence

# Strategy-preserving Linux RunAs remediation - revision 1

## 0. Review scope, status and goal
This is a decision proposal dated October 9 2026 UTC, not implementation, architecture approval, completed requirements, test success or deployment. ## 1. Isolated worktree and provenance

## 2. Requirements/approval and change impact
Through matching plugin effective/layer/readback workflow, revise existing FR-MCP-RUNAS-001/TR-MCP-RUNAS-001/TEST-MCP-RUNAS-001 without deleting history or satisfying AC prematurely. ## 3. Contracts and DI (lock before mocks)
Move existing strategy/session/request/resolver contracts from internal Services ownership to McpServer.Common.AgentCli with public XMLDocs retaining namespace for source compatibility. Put process-based strategy implementations into new McpServer.AgentExecution project (net10.0), referencing Common.AgentCli and existing logging/DI packages only. IAgentExecutionStrategy retains Name and CreateSessionAsync(request,ct); add Capabilities record DelegatedIdentity(bool), Interaction(Batch|Interactive). Capabilities are strategy-owned, policy approval separate. CLI four=true; hosted=false. IAgentExecutionSession retains all seven methods and IsAlive/ProcessId. No method returning raw server Process introduced. Common typed AgentExecutionException has code enum StrategyUnknown,IdentityInvalid,IdentityDenied,CapabilityUnsupported,WorkerUnavailable,PolicyMismatch,ProtocolViolation,OutputLimit,CleanupFailed,SessionExpired,Busy; message constant-safe, correlation ID; rejected secrets/prompt/path never included.
Add IAgentSessionTransport.ConnectAsync(AgentExecutionSessionRequest,DelegationProfile,ct): ValueTask<IAgentExecutionSession>; IExecutionIdentityProvider.ResolveAccountAsync(name,ct): (canonicalName,uid,gid,home); IAgentExecutionSettingsResolver.Resolve(selectedStrategy,callerDefaultStrategy,legacySettings,explicitOverrides): resolved path/model/profile/runAs. Singleton stateless resolvers/options; per-created-session mutable state, owned transport lifetime; no shared mutable CLI options across requests. Worker runner composition uses ONLY local CLI factory and does not register decorator/transport; fail startup if any remote decorator registered. Hosted registration never starts worker. All callers resolving strategies automatically receive same decorator. Direct Common CLI client cross-account request must throw before local spawn; process environment loading alone never authorizes Linux identity.

## 4. Configuration schema/migration
New Mcp:AgentExecution: Strategies map keyed by canonical strategy: {AgentPath:string?,Model:string?,DelegationProfile:string?}; DelegationProfiles map {SocketPath:absolute,TargetUser:string,ExpectedUid:uint,ExpectedGid:uint,PolicySha256:string}. All actual values discovered/captured during contract inventory BEFORE tests; unresolved default stops approval, not deferred implementation judgment. Prefer nullable opt-in settings to changing AgentCliClientOptions default for all unrelated consumers.
Precedence explicit session override > caller legacy path/model ONLY when selected==caller configured default > strategy entry > strategy intrinsic default. Legacy applies to its associated default, never another selected strategy. When both strategy setting and same caller legacy nonempty, retain legacy precedence and emit safe deprecation notice; automatic migration writes explicit strategy entry and removes only task-approved matching legacy fields, preserving unrelated caller differences via caller-scoped strategy override map if values differ; conflicts require no data loss, caller override wins. Path/model are independent; explicit auto means no model argument only per strategy semantics. Validate key aliases normalized once; conflicting alias/canonical duplicates startup error. No basename guessing for explicit executable; mismatch delegated policy fails, never rewrite silently.
AgentHelp.RunAs is nullable string: null (including absent YAML) inherits TodoPrompts.RunAs; empty/whitespace disables; nonempty trimmed canonical account. Voice preserves existing TodoPrompts identity inheritance. TODO own RunAs preserved; pool/triage use their existing source if present, otherwise empty (do not introduce automatic sharpninja identity to every feature). Per-request parameter/env cannot set identity. For delegation, no API key/GH token/environment map passed over socket in v1, and caller configured injection => explicit IdentityDenied; local behavior remains. All caller sources inventoried before mock gate; any direct process caller configured Linux RunAs must verify same UID or reject until routed, never ignore.
Windows uses unchanged profile-environment mechanism; document not Unix impersonation. Other unsupported OS + nonempty RunAs fails capability; empty remains local. Linux account resolution failure -> IdentityInvalid, same effective UID verified -> local, other UID -> admin profile lookup and remote; no fallback. Model/executable requested must match selected policy entry; an explicit path equal approved source path is permitted, maps to policy-installed canonical artifact. No session-defined arbitrary executable admitted remotely.

## 5. Worker boundary and containment
New projects McpServer.AgentWorker (broker) and McpServer.AgentWorker.Runner (per-session local-strategy host) reference AgentExecution/Common only. Broker runs as target sharpninja in a user service under systemd --user; root-owned installed application/policy. Worker policy /etc/mcpserver/agent-worker/sharpninja.json root:root 0644; parent directories root-owned non-writable by mcpserver/sharpninja. Socket /run/mcpserver-agent-worker/sharpninja.sock directory target:worker-client-group 0750, socket target:worker-client-group 0660; group grants only mcpserver access, not arbitrary users. Actual authorized peer UID list explicit; same-account adversaries are outside Unix UID authentication guarantee. Broker checks SO_PEERCRED authorized UID before bytes; MCP checks socket parent ownership/mode/no symlinks and connected peer uid=profile ExpectedUid, not pathname alone. Policy SHA from admin profile must equal broker hash; mismatch fail.
Trust disclosure: target account owns its auth and can execute arbitrary software independently; this is bounded cooperative-agent lifecycle containment, NOT sandbox of malicious sharpninja or malicious CLI code. Do not claim cgroup prevents target user escaping to other user-manager units. Exe profiles are root-owned immutable CLI runtime snapshots staged by deployment, including launch script/interpreter/npm dependency closure for node shim tools; source-path alias maps approved original executable to installed manifest. Snapshot hash and permissions verify entire closure, refuse unresolved runtime/symlink dependency. User authentication remains user-owned; no credential copies, worker storage is not secret store. Workspace is canonical approved registered root and inode/symlink rules deny traversal aliases; workspace remains writable for real agent behavior only per existing strategy permission flags, no added always-approve. Target profile credential access is operator-approved.
Child environment is constructed empty then policy keys HOME,USER,LOGNAME,PATH,TMPDIR,XDG_RUNTIME_DIR,DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS,LANG only. HOME account database result; PATH snapshot runtime/bin plus /usr/bin:/bin, TMPDIR private mode0700 runtime. No inherited LD_*,NODE_OPTIONS,DOTNET_*,GH_TOKEN,model key or proxy variables. Model credentials read normally from target profile. Root-protected startup rejects unknown policy fields/invalid limits; bind session to policy revision; policy change drains old sessions then restart, no live partial reload. Validate immutable executable tree before startup and each spawn; directories not writable by caller/target to close writable-binary TOCTOU. Workspace canonical root plus user-trusted mutable contents is disclosed; policy validates root handle but does not promise immutable repo content.
Containment is implemented through injected IAgentProcessSupervisor; Local supervisor wraps existing spawner unchanged for nondelegated. Worker supervisor builds ProcessStartInfo with strategy argument list but launches using root-protected generic process runner through target user manager; no separate vendor CLI logic. API: StartAsync(AgentProcessLaunch,ct)->IAgentProcessLease; lease exposes ISpawnedProcess streams/status and CloseAsync(reason,timeout) returning CleanupReceipt; verified cleanup required before returning terminal result. Launch includes executableProfileId,argument vector FROM selected strategy, private working resource root; never receives raw request argv. Strategy still creates/reads its prompt/output files on target side; supervisor tracks private resource paths for crash recovery.
Per-session runner hosts the selected LOCAL CLI strategy and remains alive in Type=exec transient unit with ExitType=main, KillMode=control-group, TimeoutStartSec=10,TimeoutStopSec=5,RuntimeMaxSec=14410, NoNewPrivileges=true. Batch CLI invocations are launched in separate per-invocation transient units with generic process runner holding unit active after child exit until cleanup; interactive CLI has one invocation unit lasting its session. Process runner accepts only broker/runner internal validated launch frame, reports ready without launching, waits for ACK after exact unit/PID/cgroup capture, then launches requested strategy-built command. Actual CLI UID and PID captured before output accepted. No use of shell eval. Strategy process spawner adapter supplies pipes via existing ISpawnedProcess (sync Spawn compatibility bridged with bounded startup only; no async-over-sync deadlock on synchronization context). Isolated API contract/mock tests validate this adapter before code; timeout cancels pending start and cleans exact unit even if PID unknown.
Identity/cgroup ready deadline 10s; manager queries 2s each; start ACK once; terminate SIGTERM then manager SIGKILL with TimeoutStopSec5; stop verification 10s total; final drain5s. CLI operation deadline min(requested finite timeout, profile budget); default policy maximum14400s; helper120s preserved; negative timeout except infinite sentinel invalid. Independently enforced RuntimeMaxSec for child unit = permitted run budget+15s; idle interactive max1800s; session hard lifetime14400s. Units named mcp-agent-<policy-profile>-<epoch>-<session>-<invocation>. Generate no caller unit names. Before listening/recovery, sweep only owned prefix units and recorded resources, resolve pending start jobs, verify cgroups empty then delete resources. Cleanup failure stops admission and marks health unhealthy; normal final result not released before invocation cleanup for batch. Interactive keeps process alive until Escape (strategy semantics) or End; End verifies unit stop/descendants/files. On worker crash independent manager timer bounds lifetime, replacement worker must sweep before listen; user-manager/kernel unavailability blocks guarantee and requires operator recovery, no false completed receipt. Reparent/double-fork within unit tested; malicious deliberate cgroup escape outside claim.
Receipts contain epoch/session/op/invocation/profile/strategy/UID/PID/cgroup/exe-manifest hash/exit/cleanup booleans and times, never prompt/token/environment values. Success requires actual agent exit/result semantics and verified cleanup, not EOF/runner exit/PID disappearance. MemoryMax1GiB,TasksMax256,CPUQuota200%, one active operation globally, eight authenticated connections incl idle sessions, no unbounded queue; excess Busy explicit. Profile can lower but not increase compiled ceilings without new reviewed policy change.

## 6. Wire protocol and session semantics
One authenticated socket connection owns one session; no reconnection/resume/re-execution in v1. UUID session assigned worker, invocation per CLI execution, caller operation ids strictly monotonic UInt64 starting1 (control ids independent channel sequencing). Client is trusted MCP but all bytes validated. Frame 4-byte big-endian length then strict UTF8 JSON, camelCase ordinal keys, reject duplicates/unknown fields/NaN, maxDepth16, request<=1MiB, control<=16KiB,event<=64KiB. 5s absolute frame transfer deadline begins at first header byte (idle waiting for next frame governed session idle deadline, not five-second polling timeout); handshake10s from accept. Hello request {version:1,profileId,policySha256,selectedStrategy,workspaceId,model:string|null,agentName:string|null,initialPrompt,timeoutMilliseconds:long|null}; null timeout means profile max; target user/executable/env/outputPath are NOT payload fields. WorkspaceId maps to exact canonical root, executable profile selected by strategy policy. Client explicit path canonical policy-alias equality validated before hello and worker never uses caller path for execution. HelloAck {version,epoch,sessionId,policySha256,strategy,capabilities,workerUid,sequence:0}. Initial prompt stored privately; selected strategy creates session using requested prompt after ACK; interactive may launch immediately. Client rejects changed strategy/hash/UID.
Command envelope {version,epoch,sessionId,operationId,kind,body}; kind InitialRead,InitialStream,Send,SendStream,Escape,Cancel,End. Send body {prompt,timeoutMilliseconds}; read body {timeoutMilliseconds}; Escape body {}; Cancel body {targetOperationId}; End body {timeoutMilliseconds}. No malformed optional union fields accepted. Event {version,epoch,sessionId,operationId,sequence,kind,payload}; ProcessStarted {invocationId,agentPid,agentUid}; Output {stream:stdout|stderr|body,text}; ResultStart {state:Success|Error|Timeout|SpawnError,exitCode,contentType}; ResultChunk {field:body|stdout|stderr,text}; ResultEnd {cleanupReceiptId}; OperationCancelled {}; Error {code,correlationId}; SessionEnded {cleanupReceiptId}; State {alive,agentPid:null|positive,sessionStatus}. Result fields chunked, cap16MiB aggregate per op across body/stdout/stderr including duplicated representation; output callback streamed separately counts same raw bytes once in capture accounting, stored result fields count actual memory. Parsed is NOT serialized polymorphic CLR object: reconstruct existing parser from body/contentType, semantically same JSON/YAML parsed structure; typed data preservation tests mandatory.
First InitialRead or InitialStream consumes initial response exactly once; repeat=>ProtocolViolation. One response operation active per session; concurrent second returns Busy, no queued execution; global operation slot likewise. Send allowed only after initial operation returns successfully/nonfatal agent result and according to underlying strategy IsAlive semantics (batch permits another invocation even if IsAlive=false); Send does not require persistent process. Stream mode forwards existing yielded strings exactly, no fabricated token granularity; transport converts result/output events without double delivery. IAgentExecutionSession.AgentOutputReceived callback remains local callback replay for policy-approved outputs, not transmitted delegate; callback exceptions cancel op and clean session. Escape delegates current strategy method, no-op for strategies currently no-op; it is not transport cancellation. Cancel idempotent target current op; first terminal outcome wins cancellation/completion race under session lock. Cancellation of consuming operation sends Cancel, awaits bounded cleanup independent of caller ct, then throws OperationCanceledException locally. End/dispose idempotent, terminate active op/session; receive cleanup before acknowledgement. Client disconnect or stream-consumer abandonment cancels and ends session; no background orphan. Transport failures never retry an agent prompt automatically.
State machine Opening -> Open -> Active -> Open, or any live state -> Closing -> Closed/Faulted. Initial response consumed marker independent state. Batch process finished then PID retained as last observed agent PID, IsAlive false; next Send transitions PID on started event. Remote synchronous properties are latest observed snapshot, false/null before first started, no network query; heartbeat3s during active process, missing9s marks unknown-as-not-alive and cancels session (not proof process exited); operations surface WorkerUnavailable. One terminal event per op, sequence increments strict; duplicate/out-of-order/epoch mismatch closes and cleans; consumed op ids retained for current connection only, duplicate may return safe ProtocolViolation never rerun. No durable reconnect replay claim. Worker read and control handling independent bounded tasks; outbound queue max4events=256KiB, output total16MiB, stall frame deadline -> cleanup. Redaction constant transport/policy errors, never log requests/argv containing prompts or secrets.

## 7. BDPv4 increments, mock validation and evidence
I0: capture requirements/effective mappings, branch/hunk provenance, full interface/settings defaults inventory, approved plan+Claude architectural HV, baseline test manifest; no product code. Missing auditing/exports stop before I1; parent cannot repair separate MCP failure by bypass.

Do not claim contract compiler errors meaningful red. Prove deliberately wrong mock observable behavior causes assertion failures using Assert.Throws against same contract helper, these negative harness tests themselves pass. Each planned real-red test named below, purpose observable functionality not compile. UTC review date: 2026-10-06; exact persistence timestamp in .persistence.json.
Reviewer: Cline, IndependentHostileReviewer. API host does not expose an independently verifiable model version; plugin reports `cline`.
Classification: project design only, not implementation completion. No recursive delegation.

## Verdict

**OverallVerdict: DISAGREE. Design gate: FAIL.** A separate-account worker is a defensible direction, but the plan is not decision-complete enough to approve for execution.

- Accuracy: **94/100**. Identity diagnosis and hardening are supported; shared-strategy scoping and compatibility claims are ambiguous, source anchors are stale, and existing updater recovery must not be overread.
- Completeness: **82/100**. Good protocol/security/acceptance coverage, but unresolved caller scoping, descendant lifetime, connection admission/backpressure, existing option semantics, two-unit recovery, and persisted RunAs traceability.
- Counts: **PASS 5, FAIL 6, UNKNOWN 3**. Both scores FAIL the >=98 approval threshold. Scores assess design approval readiness, not absent worker code. No goal/TODO/requirement/plan done-state is authorized.

## PASS

**P1 - Honest scope and approval boundary.** Plan lines 5,34-53,200-205 describe a proposal, disclose delegated sharpninja access and non-sandbox status, and require explicit operator approval. No deployment claim. No worker is expected yet; its absence is not a FAIL.

**P2 - Linux diagnosis and server boundary verified.** `ProcessEnvironmentService.cs:30-33` returns on non-Windows. `GrokCliAgentExecutionStrategy.cs:205-230,320-352` creates the prompt in-server and uses a normal ProcessStartInfo without UID transfer. `DefaultProcessSpawner.cs:12-16` calls Process.Start. `/etc/systemd/system/mcpserver.service:10-16,23` specifies mcpserver and NoNewPrivileges=true. Live systemctl: MainPID=3005734, User=mcpserver, Group=mcpserver, NoNewPrivileges=yes. `/proc/3005734/status`: UID/GID 958 throughout, NoNewPrivs=1. `id`: sharpninja UID/GID 1000; mcpserver 958. This proves current server identity, not future worker identity.

**P3 - Useful protocol restrictions.** Plan lines 75-99,107-132 specify bounded length-prefixed JSON, forbidden command/environment/path fields, SO_PEERCRED before payload, root-owned policy, exact workspace, model allowlist, private create-new prompts, and resource-limit failure. Lines 49-53 correctly disclaim sandboxing. The installed Grok path is a symlink to its npm package; the plan explicitly trusts the user-owned executable. Root-owned policy does not mean a root-owned Grok binary.

**P4 - Real answer acceptance.** Plan lines 7-10,173-198 require deployed defaults, completed helper answer with expected FINAL ANSWER content, correlated actual child UID, unchanged MCP identity, and cleanup receipts. `AgentHelpConversationService.cs:643-689` distinguishes answers, progress-only output, failure and diagnostic-only echo. Effective FR/TR/TEST-MCP-TRIAGEHELP-001 reinforce this. No helper acceptance is claimed here.

**P5 - Intended phase/change discipline.** Plan lines 134-181 require Nuke deployment, preservation, object-based YAML mutation, requirements/AC before red tests, independent phase reviews, and full current/prior unit suites with zero failures/skips. These are future gates, not executed results. add-profile was invoked first and all 19 non-add-profile global markdown files read. Review used pwsh.exe and the Cline wrapper; no product/configuration or done-state mutation.

## FAIL: decision-complete design approval blockers

**F1 - Helper-only scope is not encoded (high).** Plan lines 62-68 exclude TODO, triage, voice, persistent sessions and other strategies, but lines 78-79 select remote sessions using grok-cli plus Linux RunAs alone. The shared request record has no helper-purpose discriminator (`IAgentExecutionStrategy.cs:48-53`); the Grok strategy is registered in shared DI (`:119-128`); AgentCliClientOptions.RunAs is generic (`:50`). The predicate cannot distinguish included from excluded callers. This is ambiguity, not an assertion that absent code misroutes. Decide a helper-only capability/purpose or separate adapter and test all excluded callers. Define other strategies with configured RunAs; a session strategy override must not silently defeat an identity guarantee.

**F2 - Descendant-lifetime promise exceeds the mechanism (high).** Plan lines 101-105/AC5 promise no detached job survives, using process-tree kill and systemd KillMode=control-group on worker shutdown. Existing `DefaultProcessSpawner.cs:48` uses Process.Kill(entireProcessTree:true). An ancestry-based kill does not durably retain reparented descendants or children after root exit. Shutdown of the long-lived worker does not establish per-invocation cleanup while it remains running. Decide OS-backed invocation containment, such as a managed cgroup/unit or equivalent proven mechanism compatible with NoNewPrivileges. Require real-process normal-exit, double-fork/reparenting, inherited-output-handle, disconnect/cancel, crash and cleanup-failure tests; gate success on cleanup. This is lifecycle containment, not arbitrary-code sandboxing.

**F3 - Connections and blocked replies are not bounded (high).** Plan lines 82-105 cap frames/output, one active invocation, handshake and run time, but omit maximum accepted/pending sockets, pre-handshake concurrency, queue policy, duplicate-ID retention and outbound write/drain deadlines. An authorized peer can accumulate idle sockets or stop reading after launch; one active child does not bound those resources. Decide immediate busy rejection versus bounded queue, connection/replay-cache limits, and read/write/drain deadlines. Cancellation must progress despite a non-reading peer. Add flood, partial-frame and blocked-reader AC/tests.

**F4 - Existing helper option compatibility is undecided (medium/high).** Current helper forwards ModelApiKey and session AgentParameters into EnvironmentVariables (`AgentHelpConversationService.cs:791-798`); AgentHelpOptions exposes the key/variable (`:39-48`); helper accepts session AgentPath/model (`AgentHelpConversationService.cs:775-788`). Worker forbids client environment/executable fields (plan 85-87) and uses sharpninja authentication. Reasonable security policy, but changed option semantics. Lines 69-71 disclose only previously ineffective RunAs changes. Decide fail-closed handling for configured keys, session parameters/path overrides, timeout sentinels and models outside policy. Document compatibility and tests: no silent dropping, secret forwarding across accounts, or local fallback. Current methods are BuildAgentCliOptions and ExecuteHelperAsync, not stale plan anchors BuildAgentOptions/RunHelperAsync.

**F5 - Recovery lacks a two-unit transaction design (high).** Plan 136-155 promises registration and restore of units/config/build through Nuke, but does not define the state machine. Current `Build.UpdateService.cs:212-267` publishes one apphost and updates one service. `LinuxServiceHelper.cs:49-54,77-85,121-131` preserves selected live state and explicitly says no binary rollback was performed on failure. A future extension is possible, but essential. Decide prior binary/manifest backup, both units/policy, first-install rollback when units were absent, socket activation stop/start order, active invocation disposal, enabled/masked state restoration, shared lock, crash/failure checkpoints, and worker-success/MCP-helper-failure recovery. Map failure-injection tests. Restored YAML or one healthy service is not full rollback.

**F6 - RunAs traceability remains proposed (phase-1 readiness).** Plan 12-14 proposes FR-MCP-RUNAS-001, TR-MCP-RUNAS-001, TEST-MCP-RUNAS-001. Supplied effective snapshot and supported-wrapper refresh are layer-1: 338 functional, 461 technical, 492 testing; zero RUNAS IDs in each and zero RUNAS mapping matches. Plan AC1-AC7 are not authoritative stored RunAs AC/mapping entries. Link new records to existing HELP-010/011, TR-HELP-010, TRIAGEHELP-001 and SERVICEUPDATE-001, with F1-F5 decisions, through supported client before phase 1 passes or tests/implementation start. This is not demanding passing implementation tests for a concept. Reviewer did not create requirements: review-only authorization.

## UNKNOWN: prerequisites, not invented implementation failures

**U1 - Explicit architecture approval remains outstanding.** Plan 38-40,202 and user expressly say so. Implementation stays unauthorized until approval is recorded. This is a before-implementation blocker, not proof the concept is invalid. Independent review cannot substitute for operator approval.

**U2 - Future runtime outcomes unverified.** Worker authentication, hooks/network access, separate-UID socket operation, Grok UID, prompt ownership and cleanup remain future integration/deployment checks (plan 126-148,200-205). No worker project was found in reviewed src scope; no Grok/helper was launched. Define secret-safe preflight and exact required environment. Missing worker/runtime/full-suite receipts at a design-only gate is not itself FAIL.

**U3 - Source/deployed equivalence and live defaults unverified.** Named source is in a preexisting dirty working tree. R2-F1: The remediation selected the 34 tests that failed in the round-one sandbox, rather than all tests that exercise a native or environment boundary. Two remaining unit tests create real symbolic links and assert native reparse-point handling. Both passed on these hosts, but their success still depends on actual filesystem link capabilities. The fake process runner in the second test does not fake its filesystem. Two additional unit cases locate and read repository files outside their test output, beyond the two source-reading guards declared by D-C. Sandbox success is not a proof of environmental independence. Change required: Classify the surviving native contracts as Category=Integration, untagged when applicable on both hosts, preserving assertions, or isolate the actual filesystem boundary with deterministic fakes. Sweep siblings by dependency, not by whether a particular sandbox run failed. Resolve the two additional repository-dependent cases with fixed fixtures or integration classification and lane inclusion, and make the source-reading exception inventory exact. Reconcile counts and rerun full gates on both hosts. Keep the USECASE platform criteria and the D-B conditional group unsatisfied until the complete rule is evidenced.

R2-F2: The lexer now preserves interpolation expressions, but subsequent line-based matching still misses an OperatingSystem member call split after the dot. SupportedOSPlatform matching also misses globally qualified attributes and attributes later in an attribute list. These are direct executable or attributed test constructs, not the declared helper or BCL blind spots. The strengthened guard therefore does not implement the stated direct-platform-check contract. Change required: Add these direct-syntax cases and rejection controls to the scripted mock harness, then make platform matching handle whitespace across lines, global qualification and attribute lists while retaining literal/comment exclusions. Bind the same cases to the real scanner, preserve the documented helper limits, and prove a full green mock gate before the corresponding binding/classification slice and then full final gates.

R2-F3: The self-review says every script designed or run in round two was checked by Invoke-Analyzer.ps1 before running. Start-WinInteractiveLane constructs a separate runner as strings, writes that .ps1, and starts its scheduled task without parsing or analyzing the emitted file. The recorded analyzer commands check the parent launcher and read-back scripts, not the generated runner. Analyzing string literals in the parent is not analysis of the generated program. The disclosed exceptions do not include this gap. Change required: Correct the self-review and any blanket propagation claim to disclose that the generated runner was not independently analyzed before that historical execution. Retain the original receipts. Analyze the actual emitted script before future execution. A later analyzer result must be described as later, never as retroactive pre-execution evidence.

## 6. Supervisor, broker-session-invocation protocol and containment
Broker AgentWorker, session host AgentWorker.Runner, generic invocation runner. Session host uses SAME local CLI strategy and supervised IProcessSpawner/ISpawnedProcess. Broker owns durable registry of generated session/invocation/unit/resource IDs, fsync BEFORE systemd submission or file creation. Session runner sends AllocateInvocation{epoch,sessionId,operationId,launchDigest,resourceNames}; broker derives invocation UUID/unit/lease, saves, replies Allocated. ONLY then session runner invokes systemd-run for exact registered unit; broker monitors Submitted/Ready and sends ReadyApproval after identity. Crash between registration/submission: inspect exact unit AND pending start jobs; absent unit alone not proof. Read errors disable admission. AllocResource/AllocatedResource same registry-first file creation, private dir0700/file0600.
Broker/session internal pipes carry SessionStart{profileHash,strategy,workspaceId,model,silent,initialPrompt,remainingLifetime,callerLane}, SessionCommand/Event same public schemas, AllocateInvocation/Allocated, AllocateResource/AllocatedResource, UnitReady/ReadyApproval, InvocationExit/CloseReceipt, SessionFault. Authenticated connection epoch/session and monotonic operation IDs on all. Broker launches session unit only after registered; session launches invocation only after broker registration and runner readiness approval. Internal launch uses strategy-generated args, never public raw argv.
Invocation pipe frames Ready{runnerPid,startTicks},StartAck,ProcessStarted{agentPid,inheritedUid/Gid,invocationId},ChildExit{exitCode},StdoutBytes/StderrBytes/StdinBytes{base64},StdinClose,Escape,Cancel. All pipes 4-byte big-endian length plus strict UTF8 JSON; control frame cap1MiB (Launch/SessionStart), byte frames64KiB with raw chunks32KiB, base64<=43692+envelope. No conflicting universal256KiB cap. Unknown/duplicate fields, invalid epoch/order rejected. CLI raw pipes distinct from control; multiplex backpressure256KiB per stream; UTF8 split handled by StreamReader, not per chunk decode; launcher stderr bounded separate. True direct agent PID and child exit semantics, not systemd-run PID. CLI text cannot spoof protocol.
systemd-run --user --pipe --wait --unit generated with Type=exec,ExitType=main,KillMode=control-group,TimeoutStartSec=10,TimeoutStopSec=5,RuntimeMaxSec=remaining+15; feature preflight target systemd261. Runner held Ready before child launch max10s; query exact MainPID/ControlGroup within2s, match PID/start ticks; actual UID from /proc/MainPID/status BEFORE ACK, not empty user-unit UID property. Verify gid/cgroup, failures never launch. Broker ReadyApproval permits one StartAck. Child identity inherits verified runner under trusted code/NoNewPrivileges; ProcessStarted receipt plus reaped exit survives fast exits, optional proc child sample not prerequisite. No output before ProcessStarted. Start job10s, partial frame5s, stop10s, drain5s bounds.
Persist ChildExit -> stop WHOLE invocation unit -> verify completed stop/no pending starts/cgroup empty -> bounded drain -> bounded output parse -> remove registered files -> batch ResultEnd. Runner holds after child exit until stop; manager hard timeout still bounds descendants/inherited pipes. WaitForExitAsync/HasExited/ExitCode observe child, not runner. Interactive response does not require exit/cleanup; End terminates invocation. End/disconnect/crash stops all registered sibling invocation units AND session unit. Manager/kernel unavailable means CleanupFailed/admission closed, not fake proof. Capture unit receipts BEFORE reset-failed; explicit reset-failed recorded unit after proof then verify unloaded (CollectMode inactive, never GC before receipts). Unit absence counts only known stop+prior capture, not EOF/PID absence.
Replacement broker sweeps registry/pending jobs/files before listen; private registry readable only target, separate from root installer state. Cleanup failure retains files/receipts for recovery, lane admission disabled. Test fork/reparent/inherited pipes, fast exit500, broker/runner crash, pending start/read/query timeout, output/drain caps. Runtime lifetime cooperative supervision not hostile-target containment. Receipts epoch/session/op/invocation/lane/UID/PID/cgroup/policy/runtime hashes/exit/cleanup/time, never prompts/secrets.
## 7. Public session wire and substitution
One authenticated socket owns one session, no resume/replay/reconnect execution. UUID epoch/session/invocation; operation UInt64 monotonic from1; independent control sequence. Strict UTF8 JSON camelCase ordinal, reject duplicate/unknown keys/NaN, depth16; 4-byte big-endian size; request1MiB/control16KiB/event64KiB, first-byte partial-frame deadline5s (idle separate), handshake10s. Hello{version:1,profileId,policySha256,selectedStrategy,workspaceId,model nullable,agentName nullable,silent,initialPrompt,timeoutMilliseconds nullable,callerId}; broker maps caller lane by root-approved identity, never public API arbitrary callerId. No target UID/raw executable/env/output-path fields. HelloAck{version,epoch,sessionId,policySha256,strategy,capabilities,workerUid,sequence:0}; caller rejects mismatch before strategy start.
Command{version,epoch,sessionId,operationId,kind,body}: InitialRead/InitialStream{timeoutMilliseconds},Send/SendStream{prompt,timeoutMilliseconds},Escape{},Cancel{targetOperationId},End{timeoutMilliseconds}. Event same envelope + sequence/kind/payload: ProcessStarted{invocationId,agentPid,agentUid};Output{stream:stdout|stderr|body,text};ResultStart{state:Success|Error|Timeout|SpawnError,exitCode,contentType};ResultChunk{field:body|stdout|stderr,text};ResultEnd{cleanupReceiptId};OperationCancelled{};Error{code,correlationId};SessionEnded{cleanupReceiptId};State{alive,agentPid nullable,sessionStatus}. Parsed reconstructed existing parser from body/contentType, no arbitrary CLR polymorphism. Per-op16MiB actual stored aggregate incl duplicate result representations; live output callback raw bytes counted once in capture, result memory bounded. Stream exact existing yields/no fabricated token granularity or double delivery. Callback exceptions cancel/close.
Initial response consumed once; repeat ProtocolViolation. One response op active; second Busy, no queue. Batch Send legal after initial despite IsAlive=false, underlying strategy behavior retained. Escape underlying behavior/no-op unchanged, not cancellation. Cancel idempotent current op, completion/cancel first terminal wins lock. Consuming cancellation sends Cancel and bounded cleanup independent cancelled token then local OCE. End/Dispose idempotent terminate active+session, cleanup ACK required. Stream abandonment/disconnect cancels and ends all units. No retry can reexecute prompt. IsAlive/ProcessId synchronized by ordered State/ProcessStarted, disconnect=>false/null; reconnect unsupported. Timeout min policy/session remaining, infinite delegated clamped and explicit approved change. Batch ResultEnd after verified cleanup, interactive response may have no cleanupReceipt yet (nullable field in ResultEnd for persistent response); SessionEnded must have receipt. Fatal identity/protocol/cleanup Error closes; ordinary agent error follows existing strategy life behavior. Hard deadline and lane capacity held through cleanup; no early release.

I0 prerequisites/provenance/canonical readbacks/approval/baseline manifest. {"host":"LAB-OMARCHY","timestamp":"2026-11-15T08:53:15.1424620-06:00","originals":[{"scope":"Global","category":"BESTPRACTICE","updatedAtUtc":{"nanosecond":500,"date":"2026-11-11T00:00:00","hour":17,"dateTime":"2026-11-11T17:04:51.0672605","minute":4,"timeOfDay":"17:04:51.0672605","microsecond":260,"totalOffsetMinutes":0,"year":2026,"utcDateTime":"2026-11-11T17:04:51.0672605Z","utcTicks":639300134910672605,"localDateTime":"2026-11-11T11:04:51.0672605-06:00","offset":"00:00:00","dayOfYear":315,"dayOfWeek":"Wednesday","second":51,"ticks":639300134910672605,"month":11,"day":11,"millisecond":67},"id":"MEMORY-BESTPRACTICE-001","createdAtUtc":{"nanosecond":0,"date":"2026-11-06T00:00:00","hour":17,"dateTime":"2026-11-06T17:42:21.067128","minute":42,"timeOfDay":"17:42:21.0671280","microsecond":128,"totalOffsetMinutes":0,"year":2026,"utcDateTime":"2026-11-06T17:42:21.067128Z","utcTicks":639295837410671280,"localDateTime":"2026-11-06T11:42:21.067128-06:00","offset":"00:00:00","dayOfYear":310,"dayOfWeek":"Friday","second":21,"ticks":639295837410671280,"month":11,"day":6,"millisecond":67},"version":4,"text":"# Best practices: engineering rules for every agent on both lab machines

One rule set, consolidated on 2026-11-06 at the operator's request from eight earlier Global memories of the two lab stores (listed under "Sources"). The operator's words are quoted under "Sources" at the end. It applies to all agents on both lab machines, LAB-OMARCHY and PAYTON-LEGION2, and across workspaces.

## 1. Code documentation: every code change

1.1. Every code change carries proper XML documentation that describes the affected code.

1.2. That documentation includes a dated change log entry listing the associated canonical requirement ids and descriptive acceptance-criterion ids, plus what changed and why.

1.3. Maintain purpose, behavior, parameters, returns and exceptions, as applicable.

1.4. Preserve earlier change log entries.

1.5. Verify every id against the canonical workspace records. Do not invent traceability or imply acceptance.

1.6. Where XML documentation is unsupported, use the language's native documentation comments with equivalent dated requirement, acceptance-criterion and change fields.

1.7. This is source documentation, not a request for per-PR release notes or an unrelated retrospective sweep.

1.8. Workspace guidance and examples: AGENTS.md and .cursor/rules/code-documentation-traceability.mdc.

## 2. Test runs: targeted after an edit, full gate set once at phase exit

2.1. After an edit, a BDPv4 mock gate or binding runs only the changed test classes, through the Nuke target TestGroups (TR-MCP-NUKE-020), never raw dotnet test.

2.2. The command: ./build.ps1 TestGroups --test-groups "<test project>:<Class>[,<Class>...]" ["<project>:<Class>..." ...] --test-run-id <run id>

2.3. TestGroups writes one TRX per project under TestResults/<run id>/groups/<project>/<project>.trx.

2.4. It selects the named classes whatever their category, but excludes cases tagged for the other platform (Platform!=Windows on Linux, Platform!=Linux on Windows).

2.5. It fails on an unknown project, a group that selects no case, a named class that ran no case, or any failed or skipped case.

2.6. The full gate set (Nuke Test, MigrationIntegrationTests, Build.Tests and ValidateTraceability, on both hosts) runs once, at the final head, to validate phase exit before hostile validation.

2.7. If a gate then fails: fix it, test the fix through TestGroups, and run the full gate set once more at the new head.

2.8. In McpServer, TestGroups is on branch fix/unit-suite-green-20261019 (PR 87) until that pull request merges into develop.

## 3. Windows paths

3.1. Use forward slashes in Windows paths (for example F:/GitHub/vice-sharp and C:/msys64/usr/bin/bash.exe), including paths handed to MSYS2 tools such as gcc, and in scripts, configs and generated build or link arguments.

## 4. Unit tests and integration tests

4.1. Unit tests and integration tests live in separate projects and are correctly tagged.

4.2. Unit tests exercise code in isolation, using controlled mocks or fakes as needed.

4.3. Any test that depends on the environment is an integration test, and is never classified or run as a unit test.

4.4. Apply this distinction to test-project ownership, category tags, Nuke groups and gates, and reported test evidence, across workspaces.

4.5. Preserve BDPv4's green, discriminating mock gates before production changes.

## 5. Emulators

5.1. When the work that needs an emulator is complete, shut the emulator down to a known state and freeze it.

5.2. Restore it from that frozen state only when active work needs it.

6.1. Create git worktrees inside the owning repository's workspace directory, never as sibling directories beside it. Example: TruckMate worktrees belong under F:/GitHub/TruckMate/.worktrees/<name>. This applies to every repository.

7.1. NuGet warnings may never be ignored.

One rule set, merged on 2026-11-06 from MEMORY-PROCESS-010 (version 2) and MEMORY-PROCESS-013 (version 1), reformatted and refined at the operator's request. The operator's words are quoted under "Sources" at the end. "Task" means one task of the plan under review (in McpServer, one implementation task of the plan's TODO). "Change under review" means the commits or edits the HV round reviews. A requirement is "in flux" when a change under review adds, changes or implements it.

## 1. Verdicts and scores

1.1. Every HV round returns an overall verdict, AGREE or DISAGREE, with an accuracy score and a completeness score. The overall verdict is AGREE only when both scores are 98 or more.

1.2. Every HV round also returns a verdict for each task it adjudicates (rule 3.2): AGREE or DISAGREE, with that task's own accuracy and completeness scores. A task's AGREE needs both of its scores at 98 or more.

1.3. The per-task verdicts are the operator's own gates. They are not extra approval gates added by an agent.

## 2. Marking tasks completed, and regressions

2.1. A task that clears its own HV AGREE is marked completed in the plan and in its TODO, through the agent's plugin. The completion cites that round's request JSONL, its response JSONL and the session-log turn that holds the verdict.

2.2. A task without its own AGREE stays open, whatever the overall verdict.

2.3. A completed task is not adjudicated again as an incomplete task. It is checked only for regression, when rule 3.3 selects it. A regression is any finding that would invalidate a completed task. A task with a regression is reopened, because no done state may stand while a failure is outstanding, and it stays open until a later round clears it again.

2.4. Every regression is called out in the review summary, by task, with the finding and the requirement it touches.

2.5. Per-task verdicts keep each round tied to the plan's tasks, which helps against scope creep.

## 3. Review scope: the requirements matrix

3.1. The reviewer builds and keeps, and returns with its verdict, a matrix of: the requirements of each task, and the requirements of each change under review. The matrix shows which requirements are in flux and which tasks share them.

3.2. An open task with at least one requirement in flux is adjudicated in full and gets its own verdict and scores (rule 1.2).

3.3. A completed task that shares a requirement in flux gets regression attention only (rule 2.3). Its result is either "no regression" or a regression finding.

3.4. A task with no requirement being adjudicated in this round is not reviewed, unless the operator requests a holistic review. This holds for open tasks as well as completed ones: an open task out of scope stays open for that round. For example, an HV midway through a plan, such as a phase gate, still sees requirements and tasks of other phases; they are out of scope for that review. The matrix still lists them, marked out of scope.

## 4. What every HV request contains

4.1. Every task of the plan under review, each with a fixed number and its state (open or completed), and the changes under review.

4.2. The requirement to return the matrix (rule 3.1), a verdict and both scores for each task adjudicated in full (rule 3.2), a regression result for each task selected for regression (rule 3.3), and the regressions called out in the summary (rule 2.4).

4.3. Rule 6 (infrastructure failures), stated explicitly.

4.4. Complete paired request and response JSONL, and the complete verdict artifacts, are kept for every round.

## 5. Interpreting findings

5.1. Reason about the context and the underlying failure pattern of each finding. Do not merely patch the cited line or satisfy the reviewer's wording.

5.2. Understand the affected user outcome and the claim the evidence is meant to support.

5.3. Verify each finding against authoritative sources.

5.4. Examine related instances and the end-to-end chain among requirements, design, implementation, tests, evidence, documentation, publication and actual deployment, as applicable.

5.5. Check whether a proposed fix and its tests address the underlying class of failure without introducing new gaps.

5.6. Keep observed facts apart from inference, unverified claims and unresolved decisions.

5.7. Preserve full review receipts, and report every FAIL and every UNKNOWN.

5.8. Apply the existing plan and review rules. Do not invent additional approval gates, and do not treat passing a replacement check as proof of the user outcome.

## 6. Infrastructure failures

6.1. Infrastructure failures have no bearing on HV AGREE when sufficient review evidence is present. Judge the requested product, plan, requirements, code, tests and retained evidence on their merits.

6.2. MCP availability, live memory-loading failures, triage submission, session-log persistence or readback, and other infrastructure failures must not by themselves force DISAGREE, lower a score or block acceptance when the needed evidence is otherwise available.

6.3. Record infrastructure failures separately, as operational issues. Use the supported failsafe and retry persistence without delaying the substantive verdict.

6.4. If a failure actually prevents access to evidence needed for a specific criterion, name that missing evidence and the affected criterion honestly. Never invent a PASS or an AGREE.

6.5. Rule 6 supersedes older profile or template rules that made infrastructure persistence or live memory loading a prerequisite for HV AGREE.

turn.response:
# Independent final runner-main design review

Reviewer: Cline/IndependentFinalDesignReviewer. October 6, 2026. Bounded fresh hostile review; no delegation, implementation, live units or host changes.

## Verdict

AGREE at design level. Accuracy: 98/100. Completeness: 98/100. These are assessed design-readiness scores, not measured runtime success. No remaining concrete blocker from the original F2 issues or authoritative F6 reconciliation was identified. Approval remains outstanding; this review does not authorize implementation, deployment, satisfaction or done state.

Plan SHA256: AF69377AE444C7E06D162EAD3958FBDEDFBFE73CFFB456B26B31A087BD87AAD3. Previous verdict: docs/receipts/hv/20261006T222043408Z-cline-revised-review/receipt.md.

## Required FIRST action: F6 reconciliation

TR-MCP-RUNAS-001 body was replaced with the current plan through the active Cline PowerShell plugin client.Requirements.UpdateTrAsync. No direct-store edits or export retry. Fresh GetTrAsync and GetEffectiveRequirementsAsync verify ordinal body equality with the immutable plan snapshot and complete direct/effective TR object equality. Every prior direct field except body is preserved, including title, priority, notes, workspace, scope, status and all structured criteria/evidence. Seven AC remain unsatisfied; status remains proposed. Effective FR record and available effective mapping collections are unchanged. The update request contains only the supported TR update fields; no mapping or status mutation was invoked. Detailed checks: verification.json, tr-before.json, tr-after.json, effective-before.yaml, effective-after.json, update-Tr.request.json and update-Tr.yaml in this receipt directory.

## Original actionable findings and resolution

- B1 / incompatible flags: fixed. The normative launch uses --user --pipe --wait --quiet --service-type=exec --expand-environment=no. RemainAfterExit=no; --remain-after-exit is expressly forbidden. Waiting is on the separate systemd-run launcher while the worker handles framed streams/control concurrently; it no longer relies on active-exited retention. Primary v261 run.c rejection of remain-after-exit with pipe does not apply to this command.
- B2 / RuntimeMaxSec disabled in active-exited: fixed. The root-owned fixed invocation runner is MainPID, remains alive after Grok exits, and only terminates at explicit cleanup or its local deadline. ExitType=main and RemainAfterExit=no keep the unit in running state rather than SERVICE_EXITED. RuntimeMaxSec therefore bounds the running interval. TimeoutStartSec=10s and TimeoutStopSec=5s address the other manager states; the runner cannot extend those timers with sd_notify. Grok exit is a separate correlated child-exit event, never inferred from launcher exit.
- B3 / pruned cgroup identity: fixed. The runner emits actual UID/PID/canonical cgroup readiness before ACK and before launching Grok. The worker compares ready identity with manager MainPID/InvocationID/ControlGroup and persists it first. A fast Grok exit cannot predate identity capture. A missing/pruned unit before ACK fails launch, not success. Filesystem absence can prove cleanup only for the previously observed matching cgroup. This avoids the old active-exited prune race documented by service.c/cgroup.c; no arbitrary guessed path or PID-only success proof is accepted.
- B4 / unbounded launch/query: fixed at design level. Manager startup has the explicit 10s bound; launch/control operations and their local deadlines, uncertain late starts, exact durably recorded unit cleanup, process kill/reap and unhealthy admission are explicitly addressed. No query or systemd-run wait may synchronously block the control reader/cleanup path. Retain those budgets as separately executable acceptance tests rather than substituting generic cancellation tokens during implementation.
- B5 / stale normative TR: fixed by the supported update and independent fresh equality verification in this review. ASCII punctuation and the new runner-transport paragraph are included in the exact persisted body. The old revision-runner mismatch receipts were not rewritten.

## Retained design checks and actionable implementation follow-through

F4 is retained: transient-unit environment is explicitly supplied rather than assumed to inherit the worker system-service environment. HOME/PATH/XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/DBUS and working-directory/umask decisions remain part of the normative snapshot. Existing F1 helper-only routing, F3 bounded admission/framing/output/replay, and F5 exclusive journaled deployment/recovery are not superseded by the runner protocol.

The framed runner transport is part of the revised contract, not raw Grok stdio. During implementation preserve strict ready/start/child-exit correlation, independent draining of both child streams, control-frame delivery under output backpressure, no Grok launch before durable ACK identity, and bounded readers/launcher reaping on EOF, truncation, output limits, crashes and manager loss. The pinned runner is root-owned but executes under the actual target account; root ownership must not be mistaken for execution as root. These are implementation checks of the specified design, not newly discovered design blockers.

Required later evidence: immediate successful/nonzero Grok exits; child descendants retaining pipes; cancellation/disconnect; no ACK; late/ambiguous start; query/stop hangs; worker/runner/manager loss; output floods; empty matching cgroup and prompt removal; separate UID and authentication/network tests. Do not accept a launcher zero exit as the child result. Do not promote AC or claim a defaults-only completed helper answer without actual correlated evidence.

## Primary sources and limitations

Fresh official v261 snapshots were fetched using bounded read-only HTTPS requests from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/systemd/systemd/v261/ : src/run/run.c, src/core/service.c, src/core/cgroup.c, man/systemd-run.xml and man/systemd.service.xml. Exact URLs and SHA256 are in sources.jsonl; retained excerpts with source line numbers are in source-excerpts.md. They corroborate flag compatibility, running-state runtime timers, non-running cgroup pruning and separate start/stop timers. No exact installed patch equivalence or runtime validation is claimed. The previous review recorded installed systemd 261.2; no live manager was queried or mutated here.

Canonical docs/Project export remains blocked by the already-reported access denial; no bypass/retry was attempted. That documentation-export operational blocker is separate from successful authoritative requirements persistence. Explicit operator approval, red/Green/full-suite zero-failure zero-skip gates, real host validation, journal recovery and completed helper acceptance remain future gates, not design defects.

## Audit and scope

Only the bounded TR documentation body and new review/audit receipts were changed. No plan edit, product edit, test execution, deployment, unit operation, linger change or goal-status promotion. Two caller audit-submission mistakes (wrong request parameter; omitted explicit planFile/todoId) and one shell quoting error were corrected; no successful submission was fabricated. Bootstrap/read-only context preceded the first durable reviewer turn, a procedure-order limitation acknowledged in the audit; durable submission then succeeded before requirement mutation. Local Cline plugin 1.108.0 PowerShell surface was used after signature and health nonce verification; no full profiles were reloaded. No tool registry clone/update was performed in this no-implementation review.

Full receipt and native-object JSONL: docs/receipts/runas-f6/revision-runner-final/receipt.md, requests.jsonl and responses.jsonl. Full verdict is submitted as the session turn response; session-final.yaml and session-final-readback.yaml plus persistence-proof.json report actual persistence/readback, not merely local write success.
